commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified, out_string() already knows the exact
string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of scanning
again in stream_zrun().

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including
non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

Use the requested precision as the scan bound for the substituted
(nil) string as well; the bounded scan stops at the constant's
terminator either way.

Closes #23019

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

tidy-up: null-terminator, NUL byte

Minor steps to improve consistency.

Prefer 'null-terminator', NUL (uppercase) byte, null (lowercase) byte.
Perfer NUL over zero.

Emit the (nil) substitution in out_string() directly; it is a
constant of known length and needs no bounded scan.

Closes #23201

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: out_string() in lib/mprintf.c substitutes the 6-byte constant nilstr for a NULL %s argument. Its two emission paths rest on one invariant: the direct stream_run() emit (which copies len bytes with no NUL-aware scan) is only used when len equals the exact length of the buffer being emitted. Commit aa19c4c changes the nil arm to latch len from the requested precision (len = prec) instead of the constant's length. Alone this is safe and behavior-identical, because that arm is still emitted through the NUL-bounded stream_zrun(), which stops at nilstr's terminator after at most 5 bytes; the commit's own rationale ('the bounded scan stops at the constant's terminator') is true on that tree. Commit 2080029 widens the direct-emit condition to also fire when str == nilstr ('a constant of known length needs no scan'). Alone this is safe and behavior-identical, because the nil arm always sets len to the constant's length there. Only in combination do they break the invariant: a NULL %s argument with an explicit precision >= 7 latches len = prec (first commit) and is then emitted through the unbounded direct path (second commit), copying prec bytes out of the 6-byte nilstr global - a global-buffer-overflow reachable from the public API as curl_maprintf("%.500s", (char *)NULL). The defect has no single home: each hunk is locally correct under the contract the other commit used to provide, so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees two correct diffs. A repair that preserves both commits' stated maintenance (the scan optimization and the tidy-up) must restore the cross-commit invariant - clamp the nil-arm length to the constant's size, or gate the direct emit on len actually matching that constant - and choosing either requires reasoning about both diffs at once; reverting or 'fixing' only the hunk visible in one commit's diff either reintroduces the other half's assumption or undoes intended maintenance.
